metaTitle: Thailand eSIM | AIS & DTAC Data Plans
metaDescription: Get online in Thailand on AIS and DTAC with a data eSIM from $0.33/day. Install by scanning a QR code and keep your own number for calls and texts.
intro: An eSIMFlys eSIM keeps your phone connected in Thailand without hunting for a shop or swapping out your physical SIM. You buy a plan, scan a QR code, and your data is ready to switch on the moment you land. Because it is data-only, your regular SIM stays in place so your usual number still handles calls and texts.
countryContext: Thailand sits in Asia and draws travellers for both short trips and longer stays, so arranging mobile data before you go makes sense. eSIMFlys plans connect to Thai mobile networks, using AIS 5G and DTAC 5G. You pick your plan ahead of time and arrive with data ready, instead of queuing for a local SIM after landing.
networkNotes: Your eSIM connects to Thai mobile networks through AIS 5G and DTAC 5G, selecting an available network automatically once you arrive. You do not choose the operator manually or need to configure anything by hand. As long as your phone is eSIM-capable and unlocked, it registers on a supported network when you switch the line on in Thailand.
connectionDetails: Thailand plans start from $0.33/day in two styles: fixed data of 1, 3, 5, 10 or 20 GB, or an unlimited-daily option that renews 2 GB every day. Validity runs 5, 7, 10 or 30 days, and some plans accept top-ups if you run low. That is enough for maps, messaging, ride-hailing, bookings and everyday browsing.
activationNotes: Install your eSIM over Wi-Fi before you fly by scanning the QR code, but leave the line switched off until you reach Thailand. Most plans begin counting from the first time the eSIM connects to a local network, not when you buy. After landing, turn on the eSIM line and enable data roaming so it can register.
whyEsim: Compared with default roaming from your home carrier, an eSIM lets you buy a set amount of local data upfront rather than relying on roaming charges. Compared with buying a local SIM on arrival, there is no airport queue, no paperwork and no swapping cards, so you keep your home number active while your data runs on the eSIM.

faqs.q: Which networks does the eSIM use, and will my phone work?
faqs.a: In Thailand the eSIMFlys eSIM connects through AIS 5G and DTAC 5G, chosen automatically once you land. It works on eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phones, most iPhone XS and newer, Google Pixel 3 and newer, and Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer. Dial *#06# to check that your phone shows an EID.

faqs.q: When does my Thailand plan start?
faqs.a: Most plans start when your eSIM first connects to a local network in Thailand, not at the moment you buy. That is why you can install it on Wi-Fi at home ahead of time. Validity then runs for your plan's window, 5, 7, 10 or 30 days, from that first connection.

faqs.q: Can I keep my own phone number?
faqs.a: Yes. The eSIM is data-only, so it handles internet while your usual SIM stays in your phone. Your regular number keeps working for calls and texts as normal. To avoid extra charges on your home line, you can leave its data roaming switched off and use the eSIM for data.

faqs.q: Which data size should I choose for Thailand?
faqs.a: It depends on how you travel. For a short trip using maps and messaging, a smaller fixed plan like 1, 3 or 5 GB may be enough; for longer stays or heavier use, 10 or 20 GB or the 2 GB-per-day unlimited-daily plan gives more headroom. Some plans also let you top up.
